sources.entry: Fluxer - Instant messaging and VoIP platform built for friends, groups, and communities (alternative to Discord). (Demo, Source Code, Clients) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: A community-maintained awesome list of projects, libraries, bots, tools, clients, bridges, and hosting resources for the Fluxer chat platform.
summary.what_it_does: This is a curated list of links rather than software. It is organized by section: client-language libraries (Python, C#, JavaScript, Go, Rust, Dart, Java, Zig, Ruby, C++), bots, tools, clients, client modifications, plugins, bridges, hosting, listing sites, self-hosting guides, and development resources. Entries are one-line descriptions with links to external projects. The README points to a CONTRIBUTING.md file for adding entries. It does not itself contain runnable code.
use_cases: Finding a Fluxer API library for a given language
Discovering existing Fluxer bots to add to a server
Locating Fluxer clients and desktop client plugins
Finding bridges between Fluxer and Discord or other chat platforms
Looking up self-hosting guides for Fluxer
Finding community directories for Fluxer instances
notable: Covers libraries in about ten programming languages for building Fluxer bots and apps
Lists bridges that connect Fluxer with Discord, Matrix, Telegram, and other platforms
Includes self-hosting resources such as a Pangolin and Newt setup guide
Lists third-party clients and desktop client plugin injectors
caveats: Link list only; the entries themselves are separate projects with their own licenses and maintenance status
Some entries are marked as unofficial, unsupported, or not endorsed by fluxer.app
The README does not state a license for the list itself
